St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firwsood, Trafford, will close down in August 2027. One mother told the BBC she feared she might not be able to get a place for her daughter at another local Roman Catholic school. The council said falling pupil numbers had made the school's finances unsustainable. St Teresa's is a state-funded school and its budget is managed by its governing body. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Salford owns the site and has a role in its governance, but Trafford Council oversees its finances, and made the decision to close it. Council documents show St Teresa's had 109 pupils in July. Of those, 21 had since left to attend secondary school, while 51 secured places at other primary schools for September. With two new reception pupils joining, the school had 39 children on its roll by the time of the council's October report. The council estimated that 24 pupils would need to move to another primary school when St Teresa's closes, with the remaining 15 moving on to secondary school. Image caption, Helen fears she may struggle to secure a place at another nearby Catholic school for her daughter Parents and teachers said they believed the proposed closure encouraged families to move their children before councillors had reached a final decision. input.evidence_text: A teenager who wrote his own terrorism manifesto and is accused of stirring up racial hatred against Jewish people and foreigners has pleaded guilty to 12 terrorism offences Damien Woolfenden, 18, formerly of Bury, admitted posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV He also posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway in 2011, on to a Telegram group Woolfenden pleaded guilty to other charges of disseminating terrorist material, as well as possessing publications useful for terrorism, including the Anarchist's Cookbook During the hearing at the Old Bailey it emerged that Woolfenden had written his own terrorist manifesto in which he said he would "wait until after an election in 2028" Remanding the 18-year-old in custody for pre-sentence reports to be compiled, Judge Cheema Grubb said she had seen "mindset material by the defendant which seems to advocate violence against groups"

title: Plans for 17-storey tower by historical Marble Arch pub rejected

input.lead: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.summary: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.evidence_text: Plans for 17-storey tower by historical Marble Arch pub rejected - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 23 October 2026 Plans for a 17-storey tower block next to a historical Manchester pub have been rejected by councillors. Developer The McGoff Group had applied to build 153 flats beside the Grade II-listed Marble Arch on Rochdale Road, which has been serving customers since 1888. The company said the scheme would deliver much-needed city centre housing and help regenerate the area. But the pub's owners argued the development threatened its future, and Manchester City Council's planning committee voted to refuse the application. In its objection, the pub said the 17-storey building would be "overbearing and oppressive" and would harm the setting of the pub. Councillors also raised concerns about the impact of the development on the Marble Arch and the lack of affordable housing in the scheme. Councillor Jon-Connor Lyons said he was "deeply concerned" about the effect on "one of Manchester's distinctive and much-loved historic pubs". A member of staff told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "We get tourists coming from all over the world who are sent here. "We have generations of families drinking here, dads and grandads and sons. You don't get places like this anymore and it's something we want to keep going." title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'

input.lead: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
input.summary: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
input.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

title: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss

input.lead: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
input.summary: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
input.evidence_text: Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas" He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk" As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs

title: Inquest hears of 'great danger' tip-off before fire murders

input.lead: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
input.summary: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
input.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

input.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

input.evidence_text: In recent weeks, a spate of vandalism has seen up to 50 houses attacked in Salford and neighbouring areas of Greater Manchester Windows have been smashed, doors ripped from their hinges and walls daubed with graffiti opposing "HMOs" The term HMO is not widely known outside housing and planning circles. It stands for "House in Multiple Occupation" and refers to properties where three or more unrelated people live, usually with separate bedrooms but shared facilities such as kitchens and bathrooms While HMOs are often associated with students and young professionals, they can also provide accommodation for people leaving prison, those recovering from drug or alcohol problems, and refugees Police in Salford have said they believe that the recent spate of vandalism aimed at HMOs in the area has been "racially or religiously motivated" The term HMO was formalised in the Housing Act 1985. Before then, and for many years afterwards, such properties were more commonly known as bedsits or lodging houses

input.evidence_text: First phase of Tommyfield Park officially opens in Oldham town centre | Oldham Council The new Tommyfield Park in Oldham town centre. Published: Friday, 23rd October 2026 The site that was once home to Oldham’s sports centre has been given a new lease of life, as the first phase of Tommyfield Park officially opens. The Mayor of Oldham, Councillor Pam Byrne, marked the occasion with a ribbon cutting on Friday 23 October, celebrating another important milestone in the transformation of Oldham town centre. The first phase of the park covers 1.5 acres, with the completed park set to span 5.7 acres when the second phase opens in 2027. The new park features open lawns, walking trails, seating areas, an amphitheatre-style terrace and space for children and families to play and enjoy the outdoors. It has been designed as somewhere people can relax, meet friends, take a break from the working day or simply enjoy some green space in the heart of the town centre. Tommyfield Park lit up at night in Oldham town centre. The park is a key part of Oldham’s regeneration plans and long-term ambition to create a greener, healthier and more attractive town centre. It will help connect neighbourhoods, support new housing developments and create a welcoming space for residents, workers and visitors to enjoy. It will also link with Snipe Gardens, which opened in June 2025 , helping to create a greener walking route between Oldham Bus Station and the town centre. As well as creating a valuable community space, Tommyfield Park continues the transformation of a site that has played an important role in Oldham’s history. Red sandstone excavated from the site has been incorporated into the landscaping, alongside sections of beech trees from Tandle Hill Country Park, giving a nod to the area’s past

Cabinet’s position was that the housing and industrial proposals were not acceptable in their current form and did not have cabinet members’ support. No planning application West of Gibfield was allocated for homes, employment and green space through Places for Everyone, which was adopted in 2024 and now forms part of the statutory development plan. The current Wigan Local Plan process cannot reverse that allocation. However, allocation does not gran Our chief executive has written to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, requesting Gibfield to be removed from the plan. We are waiting for a response Cabinet has formally objected to the proposed masterplan and made clear that it cannot support the development now or in the future Peel Land may undertake ecology surveys, ground-condition testing, environmental work and traffic or transport studies to understand the site and prepare evidence. input.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
